articles.title: Arctic Bay - Normal - Wave Race: Blue Storm Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Wave Race: Blue Storm at IGN: walkthroughs, items, maps, video tips, and strategies
articles.body:
What would a Nintendo game be without an "ice level?" Like Wave Race 64, Blue Storm lets you race through the arctic ice. Thankfully, the Blue Storm track is much more pleasing and far better designed than the predecessor's.

There are two shortcuts on the Normal version of Arctic Bay that both use natural ice ramps to cut some corners. The first one incurs two missed buoys, so it can only be used twice. Simply hit the ice ramp at 1 to bypass two buoys and save time. The second shortcut carries no penalty other than a little bit more airtime. At the point marked with 2 on the map, hit the natural ice ramp with enough speed -- or better yet, boost -- and you'll jump through the opening in the iceberg.

Given the two built-in misses, you can't skip any additional buoys, but you can can perform flips even off the tiniest ice blocks for faster Turbo and some kick-ass replays.

So many floating pieces of ice, so many routes... Here are two suggestions that you can follow, but depending on your rider of choice the results may differ. There is however a simple rule that you should keep in mind -- unless they're used as a shortcut or to build up your turbo meter, jumps will slow you down . A similar rule applies for skidding on ice. Unless you've just used a turbo, skidding on any non-water surface will cost you time. On to the racing strategy.

Use your turbo boost right at the start and head towards the first red buoy. Pass it very closely on the right so that you can avoid the ice ramp that's just behind it with little to no steering. Make a right after the second buoy.

You now have to skid over a short patch of ice. Stick to the left or right walls to stay in the water as long as possible. On the other side, another piece of ice acts as a ramp. Jump it, as going around it would cost you too much time.

Once you're past this obstacle, you will notice a shallow film of water on top of the ice. Water good, ice bad. Try to avoid ice patches as you continue on your path.

A large block will break off the iceberg to the left and cause waves. But no worries, they're of no danger.

As you pass the red buoy, make a right turn and immediately engage your turbo.

You should boost just a second before a "Miss!" appears on screen (caused by the yellow buoy to the left). Stick to the wall of the iceberg to the right, race through a narrow gap and finally jump a wide ice ramp just ahead. You will have missed two buoys, but, depending on your rider, shaved some time off your lap. Do a quick trick right after the ice ramp to start filling your boost meter, then make a right turn and head towards the two buoys around the corner.

Avoid the small ice ramp and, as soon as you've got it, turbo boost towards the hole in the ice wall in front of you. If you're too nervous, you can always go around it, but you can actually make this jump quite easily (and even without boosting). Be careful that you use the left side of the ice block as a ramp.

Push down on the stick after you clear the gap and go around the next yellow buoy. Make a wide turn and then pass the following set of buoys on the way to the finish line. Boost as soon as your turbo meter is full.

You can take the same shortcut on the following lap as well as it only costs you two misses. Pay attention to the ice piece that has fallen off during the first lap. It's now floating in the water, acting as a tempting natural ramp. On the third lap, you can use it to build up your turbo since you can't take the shortcut anymore. Or, if your turbo meter doesn't need filling, avoid it to save time.

The buoys next to the ocean liner should be a cinch. You can safely boost here, too.

The water level and obstacles remain unchanged.

The stage has an overall hazier and colder look, but all the differences to the sunny condition are merely cosmetic.

Fog and snowfall impair your vision during the first two laps, but the weather clears up.

Apart from the subtle weather differences, the level is unchanged.

Though the wave height is supposed to be twice as high, the differences between this setting and the previous ones are almost unnoticeable.

There are larger waves along the ocean liner and after the jump, but they're easy to deal with. It snows on all three laps.

The storm weather condition presents you with the worst visibility and highest waves, but anyone familiar with the course layout won't find it to be any more different than the previous weather settings.

The waves are confined to the open area around the ocean liner and the final stretch leading up to the finish line.

articles.body:
GTA 6 offers three control layouts to fit your preferences – Default, Classic, and Left-Handed - so you don’t need to stick to the default if there’s another that works better for you. There are also hidden controls ranging from switching on auto drive to getting someone in a chokehold. This official IGN Grand Theft Auto VI guide explains the differences between all three Control Schemes and teaches you how to change yours, and has tips for the best controls.

To change your GTA 6 Control Scheme, which affects how you move through the world of Leonida, start by opening the main menu by pressing the Options button ( Options ) on PlayStation 5 and the Menu button ( Menu ) on Xbox. Here, you’ll see several options; navigate down to Settings .

You should automatically be inside the Control Scheme menu when you open the Settings menu. If you’re not, tab over to it with L1 / LB or R1 / RB .

You can use the left thumbstick ( Left Stick ) or the D-Pad to scroll through the three Control Scheme options here until you find one you’re satisfied with. There’s a preview to the right that shows you each input and you can toggle which ones you’re seeing by clicking on options like On Foot, Aiming, and Land / Water Vehicles.

Once you’ve chosen your Control Scheme, simply close the menu with the Options / Menu button and it’ll save automatically. If you want to revert to the default layout, change your Control Scheme to the Default option, or press Square / X to restore the default setting.

Here’s how each input differs across all three Grand Theft Auto 6 Control Schemes, laid out below:

Note that there’s no “best” control scheme for GTA 6; it’s purely up to personal preference and comfort. None give you any kind of advantage over the other.

Click on a link below to jump to that specific Control Scheme:

Did you know you can use your door as a weapon or participate in a little road rage? While some of these tips may appear as hints when loading in, we've rounded up all the hidden controls we've found so far.

articles.title: Discharge Time Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: In Grand Theft Auto VI’s Discharge Time mission, Lucia makes it to the hospital where Jason is recovering, but he doesn’t have the luxury of
articles.body:
In Grand Theft Auto VI ’s Discharge Time mission, Lucia makes it to the hospital where Jason is recovering, but he doesn’t have the luxury of resting peacefully. This official IGN GTA 6 guide walks you through how to get Jason and Lucia out of the hospital in the challenging Chapter 1 main mission, Discharge Time.

Click on a link below to jump to that section of this guide:

Cal tells Lucia that Jason is recovering in a room on the second floor before she rushes in through the entrance. Just inside, two suspicious men are poking around, obviously looking for Jason and the bag. A cop tells them to go, but this was just the warning Lucia needed to know that Jason is in trouble.

Turn left at the entrance and head up the stairs. As you walk up, Cal texts and shares the bad news that her and Jason’s BuckMe accounts have been emptied to cover the hospital costs, leaving them broke. Keep moving ahead and take the door on the left into the intensive care unit.

As you pass through the doors, you’ll see a doctor and nurse talk about a hunter as they walk out of a room down the hall and on the left. You’ll find Jason in room 203 .

He’s in rough shape. Lucia prepares Jason to go as he protests, but there’s no time to waste. She drops the bag in his lap, gives him a gun, then they’re off. You’re now low-health Jason, equipped with nothing but that pistol , sunglasses, and a bucket hat.

What follows is a rather tough mission to escape the hospital. Checkpoints are generous though, so enjoy the ride and don’t worry too much if you get Wasted!

Lucia pushes Jason out of the room and through the hallway. A nurse stops them almost immediately, but not far behind her is a man ready to give a new meaning to violence in the workplace. Combat Focus kicks in as soon as he pulls the shotgun out of the box, giving you a very short amount of time to kill the man before he shoots you.

Lucia pushes Jason forward. A man in a black jacket and jeans emerges from a door on the left with a gun. Shoot him before he gets a chance to. Another from the door just beyond appears too, then another waits beyond the double white doors. Keep shooting them as Lucia pushes, and do it quick. Jason doesn’t have much health and goes down fast if he’s shot much.

Lucia turns left and pushes Jason into the elevator. Three enemies pass by or try to get in the elevator while Jason and Lucia wait for it to go. Shoot the men as they approach.

The ride starts up again, seemingly on a lower floor, and the first man on the kill list is idly walking around on his phone. Shoot him, but be careful not to hit the man just past him escaping through the further door. This floor has far more civilians trying to escape, so be careful not to shoot them accidentally! Killing civilians can hurt Jason’s Criminal Profile drastically.

As you approach the next set of open doors, two men appear further down the hall, one after another. After they’re down, Lucia takes a door on the left. In the next room at the top of the ramp, a man bursts through the doors, knocking Jason down and leaving Lucia to face the new assailant. Mash Square / X to fight back until she regains control of the situation.

The wheelchair is broken. Lucia plops an SMG in Jason’s lap and starts dragging him down the hall. As she does, they pass glass windows and doors where civilians are running screaming as more assailants rush in.

Try not to fire too early or you may hit the innocent folks running away. Even when it is time to start shooting at the four men, it’s best to shoot in bursts rather than spraying the room. Jason can take a few seconds to reload, and if not enough of the enemies in the room are down, they can easily kill Jason or Lucia.

If any leave the room to follow, kill them quick or they’ll get Jason when they’re at point-blank range. If you do go down here or any other time, just know that checkpoints are frequent.

Once they’re past the cafe, Lucia runs off to grab Jason a new wheelchair. Now the ride can resume as before, except now with the nice SMG upgrade.

Kill the first man you see beyond the double doors. Three more men stand on the parallel platform across the room. Kill them, but be careful not to hit the two guys who were accidentally running toward the gunfire. Lucia begins helping return fire with the now-spare pistol as they continue down the ramp and more men appear in the dim turquoise room. Kill the two men at the end of the room as Lucia starts pulling Jason back through the hallway. Stay on your guard and reload as the turquoise room disappears.

Just as it’s almost out of sight, a man in sunglasses comes around the corner wielding a shotgun. Take him out fast.

A few seconds of calm later and Jason and Lucia reach a dark ER. Lucia makes a call, pushing Jason away as she takes the SMG. Playing as Lucia, shoot the two guys on the right side of the room as soon as you’re in. Jason is on the ground which gives you some time to take this room from the safety of cover if needed.

If you walk down the ramp and to the crash cart to the right of Jason, you’ll find Adrenaline that Lucia can use. Just be careful not to get hit by the man wielding a shotgun on the far right.

As soon as all five men in the room are cleared, a scene plays immediately of Lucia putting Jason back in the wheelchair and moving on.

Be careful not to shoot the hospital security guards on the right side of the next room, instead focusing on the four men further down the way clearly looking for Jason and Lucia. Lucia reverses course and pulls Jason back through the ER. At least one or two men follow through the door, immediately followed by a guy hiding in the beds to the right of the door. Shoot all three as Lucia continues pulling Jason. She pushes him around the desk and toward another set of doors, where yet another enemy bursts through. She shifts direction moving toward another ramp as a guy loudly comes out of a lit room.

On the way up the ramp, you’ll hear more screaming. Shoot the man once he’s on the left side of the room so you don’t accidentally hit the doctor or nurse behind him trying to block the next door.

Worried about your Criminal Profile ? Throw professionalism out the window for this one. While it’s good to try and incapacitate the enemies non-lethally, it’s more important that you don’t shoot civilians. So long as you don’t sink down to the worst rating, you can increase Jason and Lucia’s ratings plenty later.

The doctor and nurse clear out of the way, allowing you to shoot through the door at the two men behind it. Lucia turns right along another path. Watch the doors beyond as a man rushes through them, shooting at Jason and Lucia. He leaves the door open, allowing you to then shoot another guy down the hallway.

Lucia takes Jason’s gun and runs off to find a ride. A brief rest later, one of Mendez’s taskforce guys finds Jason and is clearly not there to help him. As Jason is brought around and grabs the man’s shotgun, button mash Square / X to take the shotgun. You need to be precise about this next part. After the initial man is down, shoot the three guys who appear quickly in the door beyond the downed officer. Then, quickly look left toward the dark hallway and shoot him.

If you take too long with any of these guys, they’ll kill Jason. Another man enters and shoots a gas container next to Jason that sends him flying in an explosion. That officer goes down to another of the mysterious assailants. Crawl toward the gun, slowly, painfully, until the man meets his end.

Lucia gives Jason a dual upgrade of a mystery medicine and an SMG. Defend the ambulance from oncoming cop cars and the guys somehow linked to Mattia and Kat as they approach the ambulance.

The best way to stop pursing cars is by shooting out their tires or killing the driver. Disabling cars by shooting their engines works too, but it’s not as effective.

This short section fluctuates between the blacked-out SUVs of the mystery group and cops. Don’t forget to use Combat Focus to more easily shoot out car tires, though they’ll still blow if you hit the tire without the ability.

The chase comes to an end after Lucia calls out a train that blocks anyone from following the ambulance. As they get away and the mission ends, you’ll receive the update to your Criminal Profile.

Lucia and Jason escape, leaving their Key Lento life behind them. Chapter 1 comes to an end, immediately kicking off Chapter 2 – Paradise Lost .

articles.title: Crosstown Traffic Walkthrough - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Jason and Lucia get their first job working more openly with Raul and his crew in Grand Theft Auto VI’s Crosstown Traffic. This official GTA 6
articles.body:
Jason and Lucia get their first job working more openly with Raul and his crew in Grand Theft Auto VI ’s Crosstown Traffic. This official GTA 6 walkthrough offers strategies for completing Raul’s operation, as well as tips for combat.

The way you begin this meeting serves to split up Lucia and Jason and get them into position, so no matter which of the leads you start with, you’ll see the mission begin similarly (though there are mild variations to the introduction cutscene).

After meeting either Raul at the bar as Lucia or Karim at the docks as Jason, you’ll get a cutscene to introduce the mission that swaps between the two groups. Lucia and Raul talk a bit about her home life, while monitoring a higher up member of Guardia Brothers. Meanwhile Jason prepares to stalk a Guardia Brothers' boat.

Things are set into motion when the men and their boat finally arrive, prompting Jason to move. Ride the motorcycle near the water – not on the edge, but close – and follow the Guardia boat straight ahead for a while. You’ll encounter small obstacles when the dirt path intersects with train tracks. Be careful not to crash, or you might lose the boat. You’ll follow them a short distance past the tracks until you arrive at Heal Your Keel, a small boatyard. A cutscene begins as you approach the gate, shifting the mission to Lucia.

If you lose the boat you’ll have some rather disappointing contacts on the line, but won’t face any heavy repercussions. Instead, you’ll swap to Lucia’s part early.

Lucia is pushing up the stairs to train only to see the doors close behind her target, Pineapples. You must get to the next station. Start by running down the stairs, and you’ll see three conveniently stopped vehicles past the turnstile:

An electric scooter by the Vice City Metro map.

A mobility aid electric scooter by the woman on the bench

A bike by the man standing next to the highway support column

You can choose any of these three to hustle to the next station, or find another creative way to get there. Go as fast as you can toward the next station and abandon whatever vehicle you choose at the base of the station. Press the left thumbstick twice to run fast up the stairs and board the back train car as soon as the doors open. Pineapples conveniently has his back toward the train car, making confrontation so much easier. Approach and press L2 / LT to begin threatening him. Lucia throws him to the ground when he tries to grab the gun, giving her the advantage yet again. You can choose to force the cell phone in his face or pressure him when he’s on the ground (the former moves the scene along faster). He’ll make the call, shifting things to Jason.

Back at the boatyard, Jason casually approaches the Guardia men. Unfortunately, they aren't convinced by the call and quickly draw their guns, prompting the guys still on the boat to leave. You have two obvious choices for getting to the boat:

Follow on a motorcycle : Just beyond the two men taking cover with their guns is a motorcycle primed for riding. Hop on it and follow Karim’s directions to catch up to the money boat.

Follow on a boat : There’s one boat left at the dock, unlocked and ready to go. Run to it and follow the three boats ahead. Do your best to get rid of the two support boats fast as they can sink yours if they get a good shot in.

You’ll have to restart from the boatyard checkpoint if you lose the boat with the money.

When you’re on the water and can get close to the boat with the money, you can then stop it from moving by shooting the driver or jump to the boat while the driver is still operating it, then incapacitate him. No matter how you choose to do it, you’ll swap back to Lucia once you have control of the target boat.

As the metro pulls into the next station, the bystanders evacuate as three more Guardia Brothers push in, targeting Lucia. Fight the three men. The last one with the mohawk provides an opportunity for you to try and parry ( Cross / A ) a punch then follow up with a counter attack ( Square / X ). With all three men on the floor, you’ll need to stop the train by hitting the emergency stop button on the back side of the car (it’s on the north end). Mash Cross / A to open the doors, allowing Lucia to escape the metro train before more Guardia Brothers can reach her.

Jason takes the wheel, leaving Lucia to play gunner for this escape. Open the two back seats on the boat to reveal the following supplies:

Thanks, Guardia Brothers! Load up on everything and prepare to defend Jason and the boat.

If you haven’t used body armor yet, now’s a great time to see what it can do. When Jason and Lucia wear body armor, damage from gunshots and explosives goes straight to the body armor’s bar rather than Jason or Lucia’s health bar. Once the body armor is destroyed, damage is done to Jason and Lucia like normal.

Reinforcements for the Guardia Brothers roll in wave after wave on Seasharks and Lure Predators. Some also shoot from bridges above the water as Jason drives under them. Here are a few tips for successfully surviving this chase:

All guns currently in your possession have unlimited ammo. Prioritize using the ones with a high rate of fire, which are likely the assault rifles from the boat.

Use the sides of the boat for cover. The body armor can take a beating, but this is a long chase. You’ll get to keep what remains of the body armor after this if it’s not destroyed.

Watch all sides of the boat, not just immediately behind it. Some enemies will pull up alongside the boat and can do significant damage if they’re ignored too long.

After some time on the water, any remaining Guardia Brothers veer off as the Coast Guard arrives on the scene with many more boats and a helicopter. Their boats are fast and some are much bigger than yours, making shooting out the engines less feasible if that’s been your method. If shooting out the engine takes too long, focus on whoever is steering the ship. Karim has a plan to get Jason, Lucia, and the money out of this mess. He directs Jason toward a bridge that creates enough of a disturbance to stop any boats from pursuing Jason and Lucia, allowing them to escape. The mission ends on another boat, La Mano de la Suerte – Raul’s boat. Jason and Lucia don’t get many answers about Raul’s goals yet, but they do get paid $3,000 for their work.

After a short amount of time passes, Raul texts Jason and Lucia asking them to meet him at another spot in Stockyard. Next in this story mission thread is Meet Raul’s Crew .

If you’re ready to make Raul wait as payback, there’s plenty to do in Vice City – including irritating the Guardia Brothers even more by robbing their fronts and compounds. Get tips on hitting those and more with these other helpful guides:

articles.title: All Snapmatic Animal Locations (Legendary Animals) - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: This GTA 6 guide covers the locations and rewards for the 9 Legendary Animals -- or Snapmatic Animals as they are called in Grand Theft Auto
articles.body:
This GTA 6 guide covers the locations and rewards for the 9 Legendary Animals -- or Snapmatic Animals as they are called in Grand Theft Auto VI.

In addition to these 9 Snapmatic animals to hunt, there are two more you can also kill that aren't part of the set but give you big rewards from Bret. Speaking of Bret...

These missions begin in Chapter 2 where Jason's friend Bret will contact you and ask to meet. After completing the hunting tutorial with Bret, he will occasionally send Jason new "Target Decks" which will be a list of two to three animals for Jason to hunt down and turn in for money. While the Target Decks will have search areas on the map, occasionally, Bret will text Jason about an animal he heard about or encountered. Once you receive that text, a section will be added to your Activities index called Snapmatic Animals. These do not have search areas on the map but instead come with a vague clue as to where to find the animal.

You cannot just hunt down all the Snapmatic Animals using this guide page. You must have been given the clue from Bret before the animal spawns. In this guide, we will give you the clues, locations, and rewards for each of the Snapmatic Animals Bret wants you to hunt down. There are two Legendary Animals at the bottom of the page with no clues, however.

Your reward for each animal will be money, but you will get more money for a Pristine rating on a kill -- and we will recommend the weapons to use to get these clean kills.

Clue: Bret mentioned it might be found near the coast northeast of Grayson.

Location: Northeast of Grayson, along the coastline

Clue: Bret said it lurks somewhere between Wetman Bay and Cottonmouth Lake

Location: On an island southeast of Wetman Bay, west of Cottonmouth Lake

Clue: Bret said it has been seen near the 4th hole at Leaf Links.

Location: Leaf Links golf course. Northeast of Vice City, Northwest of Vice Beach.

Clue: Bret said it roams somewhere near the old radar station on Wild Hog Point

Location: West of Port Gellhorn on Wild Hog Point

Clue: Bret mentioned it can be spotted somewhere deep inside Buckskin Swamp.

Location: Buckskin Swamp, west of Vice City.

Clue: Bret mentioned it has been sighted south of Hamlet.

Location: South of Hamlet, on the southern edge of the city.

Clue: Bret said it might be prowling around some farms north of Belville.

Suggested Weapon: Hawk & Little Mediator

Location: In the farmlands north of Bellville

Clue: Bret said it has been seen near Howe Dairy in north Emerald Springs.

Location: East of Port Gellhorn, north of the Emerald River

Bret mentioned it has been seen stalking on Belpoint Island.

Location: On Belpoint island, west of Capri

The following two animals will not receive location hints from Bret, as they are not technically considered "Snapmatic Animals". Though, hunting them and returning them to Bret will net you a big reward, and they will be tracked on the Animals progress tracker.

Clue: There won't be a clue for Karkinos, but if you shoot it, send a picture of it to Bret and he will be surprised you found it and send you the money.

Location: Wetman Bay, island north of Key Lento and west of Cottonmouth Lake.

Clue: There is no clue for Gang Panther. If you deliver it to Bret, he will send you the money.

Location: Way northeast of the entire map, on the southeast side of Frampton Islands.

For more shooting activities, check out GTA 6's Shooting Ranges or regular animal hunting. You can find separate official guide pages for these activity here.

articles.title: All Riata Locations - How to Restore - GTA 6 Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Once you've restored the Transgressor, you'll be on to the second of Wyman's Cars, the '70 Riata. Here’s where to find all the Riata
articles.body:
Once you've restored the Transgressor , you'll be on to the second of Wyman's Cars , the '70 Riata . Here’s where to find all the Riata locations and how to restore this untowable project car.

The three scans for the Riata Classic can each be found in the south of the map:

Riata Scan 1 Location – Key Lento Carport

Parked beneath a gray stilt house behind the police station, opposite the impound lot, near the center of Key Lento along the north coast.

Behind the police station in Key Lento on the side of the Sunbelt Highway, you’ll find the police station's impound. Across the road from the impound, towards the coast, is a house that sits above a driveway.

You’ll find a jet-ski on a trailer in the driveway, and beside the jet-ski is the first beat-up Riata.

Riata Scan 2 Location – Southwind Carport

Parked beneath a brown stilt house on the east coast of the Southwind suburbs, east of Mile Zero Air Station, in the far south of Leonida.

Across the bridge from Key Lento is Southwind, to the east of Mile Zero Air Station. Along the main road is a Xero gas station – take a right and follow the road until it ends at the water’s edge.

South of Hamlet is a small strip of land inside of Shoeless Keys. On Old Fort Road, there’s an abandoned gas station.

Behind the gas station, underneath the gas station's car port, is the final rusty Riata.

The '67 Transgressor is the first vehicle you need to restore as part of Wyman's Cars , a type of collectible vehicle you can find if you have access to the Ultimate Edition of GTA 6 . Here’s where to find all the Transgressor locations and how to restore this untowable project car.

GTA 6 Transgressor Locations (’67 Transgressor)

The three scans for the Transgressor can each be found in and around Port Gellhorn:

Transgressor Scan 1 Location – Trailer Park

Parked outside a trailer in the middle of the trailer park at the center of Port Gellhorn, Kelly County.

In the middle of Port Gellhorn, look for the circular drive-in for McCarthy’s Fresh Fruit & Veg off the US-9 highway. Run past the right side of the building towards the trailer park behind it.

After passing the trailer on your right (and a nearby pet pig), you should see the beat-up Transgressor on a concrete slab, in the shade of some nearby trees.

Transgressor Scan 2 Location – Gellhorn Avenue

Parked in an open garage behind a blue bungalow directly west of the Stash House and northeast of Brooks Boatworks Illegal Operations in northern Port Gellhorn, Kelly County. There is a custom red pickup truck on the driveway.

In northern Port Gellhorn, to the east of Brooks Boatworks (run by Kolt & Associates) is Gellhorn Avenue. Travel north-east along Gellhorn Avenue, past the tennis courts, until you find the blue house with the green and white sunflower yard ornament.

Down the driveway, beyond the custom-detailed pickup, you’ll find a rusty Transgressor in an open shed.

Transgressor Scan 3 Location – Behind Dirt Merchants

Parked against the wooden fence next to a trailer behind the Dirt Merchants bike store in the far south of Port Gellhorn, on the northeast corner of Gellhorn International Raceway.

In the southern-most point of Port Gellhorn, you’ll find a Dirt Merchants bike store. Beside the store is a dirt road that leads to a small trailer park.

Follow the same long road all the way down until you pass a small building with an RV parked out the front. Behind that building, against the back fence, is the final rusty Transgressor.

After you’ve scanned each of these wrecks, Wyman will text you after some time has passed in-game, asking for $1,500 to pay for his labor. Once you’ve done that, you can go and collect the '67 Transgressor from his scrapyard (marked with a W symbol on the map).

Up next, the second of Wyman's cars: the '70 Riata .

articles.body:
Once you've restored the Transgressor and Riata , you'll be on to the third of Wyman's Cars , the ' 64 Mamba GT . Here’s where to find all the Mamba GT locations and how to restore this untowable project car.

Three of the four scans for the Mamba GT can be found in Kelly County, near the center of the map. The fourth scan is further north in Moreau:

Mamba GT Scan 1 Location – Gellhorn Private Residence Garage

Parked inside the garage of the gray house on the hill surrounded by fields north of Leonida State Prison, located between Emerald Springs and Gellhorn in Kelly County.

When driving north of Leonida State Prison down the highway, you’ll pass a Gruppe Sechs facility on the right. Take a left at this intersection and approach the house that’s up the hill.

Beside the house is a detached garage, and if you open either door of the garage, you’ll find a Mamba GT.

Mamba GT Scan 2 Location – Ambrosia Highway Private Garage

Parked in a pale green garage behind the Xero gas station near the center of Ambrosia, east of the Hog Stars Garage Illegal Operation and Wyatt Motors purchasable garage.

When driving through Ambrosia down the main freeway, you’ll pass a Xero gas station underneath a rainbow Tiny Frank billboard. Walk beside the gas station and the nearby tractor yard, and then travel south behind the strip of shops.

Halfway down this alley, you’ll see a small garage door next to a green trailer. Open up the garage to find the next Mamba GT.

Mamba GT Scan 3 Location – Thrillbilly Mud Club Pond

Partially submerged in the pond at the center of the Thrillbilly Mud Club in North Kelly County, east of Port Gellhorn and west of Ambrosia.

From the “Thrillbilly Mud Club – Dirt Track Races” waypoint on the map, enter the park via the big overhead sign, and then take a left, followed by another left onto the dirt track.

Not too far from here is a pond to the left of the track. In this pond is a waterlogged Mamba GT.

Mamba GT Scan 4 Location – Moreau Broken Bridge Wreckage

Partially submerged under the broken bridge east of Bonanza on the northern tip of Leonida, near the Saint Attaway Islands.

In north Moreau, near the eastern boundary of Bonanza, is a road with an old broken bridge.

Down below, in the wreckage of the bridge in the swampy water, you can find the last Mamba GT wasting away.

Once you’ve found every wreck, Wyman will request a $1,500 BuckMe payment for the work he does to restore the ’64 Mamba GT, and then you can pick it up after a short delay.

Up next, the fourth and final of Wyman's cars: the Reynolds Kit Car .

Once you've restored the Transgressor , Riata , and Mamba GT , you'll be onto Wyman's Cars final vehicle, the Reynolds Kit Car. Here’s where to find all the Reynolds Kit Car locations and how to restore this untowable project car.

The Reynolds Kit Car has 5 scans that can be found across the entirety of Leonida:

Parked in Willie's Service Center under the overpass through Salton, east of VCIA, near a large green parking garage and the Pawn City pawn shop.

In Vice City, in the south of the Salton district, is a tall, green parking lot building, north of the 7th Avenue Garage. To the west of the green parking lot, towards the highway, is an orange and blue repair shop called “Willie’s Service Center”.

The garage doors are locked, but you can smash open the side doorway into the garage. Inside the garage is the first Kit Car for you to scan.

Reynolds Kit Car Scan 2 Location – Rialto Islands Mansion Driveway

On the gated driveway of a mansion on the northern edge of Casanova Island, the eastern side of Rialto Islands that joins Vice City's Bayside with Vice Beach.

In the Rialto Islands, on Casanova Island, travel along the northern road until you come to an abandoned lot. From the street, walk over to the building beside the vacant lot on the left.

Push open the driveway doors and the second Kit Car will be sitting right in front of you in the driveway.

Reynolds Kit Car Scan 3 Location – Wild Hog Point Beach Cargo Container

In an orange shipping container on the west beach of Wild Hog Point, southwest of Port Gellhorn in Kelly County.

West of Port Gellhorn is Wild Hog Point. Drive down to the end of the airstrip here and then turn right onto the sand road. Once the beach is directly west of you, travel left off the road towards the beach, and you’ll find a bunch of discarded shipping containers by the water’s edge.

The orange container by itself on the beach can be broken into with an angle grinder. Inside it is the third Kit Car to scan.

Behind Donnie's Auto Repair in the south of Watson Bay, Mariana, between the Pay 'N' Spray and Poppers convenience store. It's just west of the Timeless Peculiars pawn shop.

In Watson Bay in Mariana County, if you travel on Seabell Avenue along the south of the town (near the Ammu-Nation and Pay-n-Spray), you’ll see a big motel leading south into the water.

Walk behind Donnie’s to find one of the Kit Cars just sitting there behind the shop.

Parked in the garage of a white and brown mansion on the northwestern tip of Capri in South Kelly County, near a mansion under construction.

On the western edge of the map is Capri. Travel along the road for the north-western outcropping. As you almost pass the construction site on your right, across the road is a mansion with two knocked-over traffic cones and two bins out the front.

Walk down the driveway, and the room with the wood trim in front of you is the garage. Break in either through the door or the garage door, and inside you’ll find the last Reynolds Kit Car.

Once again, Wyman will ask for payment, again for $1,500, and then the Reynolds Kit Car is yours!

Success, now head back to Wyman's garage and you'll be able to pick up the Born Free Deviant .

articles.title: Should You Trust Halifax in GTA 6?
articles.summary: Should you trust Halifax in GTA 6's chapter three mission, Dubious Provenance? We have the answer.
articles.body:
Warning: Spoilers for the Dubious Provenance mission in chapter three of GTA 6 follow.

GTA 6 is full of choices, big and small. In fact, the whole way you choose to play the game is a choice, whether that be as an ultraviolet psychopath or a more professional class of criminal. Or if you decide that Jason and Lucia are a couple hopelessly head-over-heels in love, or more platonic partners in crime. Some choices, however, are much more binary, with instant effects tied to them. One of the clearest examples of this is presented to you during a chapter three mission called Dubious Provenance. Should you trust Halifax or not?

The answer is twofold: the smart decision is to reject his offer, but the much more fun option is to place your faith in him. Let me explain.

Dubious Provenance kicks off by driving all the way to the fancy town of Capri, found in the east of Leonida, and home to the sort of houses Jason and Lucia can only dream of living in at this point in their story. Just by the centre of town is an antiques store where you’re tasked with bringing the mysterious statue that has fallen into your possession to be valued. Halifax, a man with a fairly convincing British accent, overhears your conversation with the shop’s owner, Evelyn, and offers you a deal. While she isn’t interested in the statue, he most definitely is, telling you that he will get it valued for you if you hand it over.

Now, despite his smart appearance, all is not what it seems with Halifax, and without spoiling it too much, he’s not exactly the antiques expert he claims to be. The smart, and arguably correct, choice from a story perspective is to reject him. But the much more fun and beneficial option (if you’re a collectibles hunter) is to accept.

Accepting adds a couple more main missions to the Dubious Provenance story rather than just ending it there and then. You’ll also receive the Crowex Octane “Bobby Ambrose” unique watch in return. This is a missable collectible otherwise. But more importantly, you get two more very fun missions to play through. The first includes a stealthy infiltration and a massive, and I mean, massive revelation about Halifax. The second is one of the best chase sequences in GTA 6, scored hilariously to a great bit of contrapuntal music. For full spoilers and a step-by-step guide, you can check out our walkthrough .

If you reject, you won’t get the watch, but you will have a second shot at playing through these missions. Halifax will later contact you and give you the option to phone him if you change your mind, transforming these main missions into optional ones. These must be completed by the end of chapter three , or they’ll disappear forever, though. Ultimately, the choice to accept or reject comes down to whether you want the watch or not. Of course, you can choose to just never contact him again if you’re desperate to progress through the story as quickly as possible, but you will miss out on a great bit of fun as a result.

So, should you trust Halifax during Dubious Provenance? I’d say yes; it’s a much more fun road to take if you’re looking to squeeze every bit of enjoyment out of GTA 6. Plus, who could ever resist a moustache like that?

articles.body:
Strip clubs are part of the very DNA of GTA 6 , and exotic dance chain Spearmint Rhino is making the most of it, hiring a choreographer to recreate the moves of the in-game dancers for its patrons. According to the club, it's in response to a wave of requests from visitors and people sliding into its DMs.

"I’m fascinated with the attention to detail from Rockstar," said the head choreographer, Brooke Wilde. "I spent hours in Jack of Hearts and Delights Cabaret, mastering each performance to bring back to Spearmint, and now obsessed gamers can put down their controllers, get out of the bedroom, and experience their favourite virtual lap dances with the Spearmint Rhino girls in the real world. While the in-game strip clubs are addictive, nothing beats the real thing.”

While we can't be sure exactly how many people are reaching out to their local strip joints for IRL GTA-inspired bodily contact, you have to respect the hustle. It's also an interesting counterpoint given GTA 6's impact on another part of the adult entertainment industry, with Mashable reporting that Pornhub saw a 15.5% drop an hour after the game was released on November 19.

Spearmint Rhino's relationship with the series actually goes back to 2013 and GTA 5, when Rockstar used a play on the name of the clubs, Vanilla Rhino, and Rockstar has said that developers for GTA 6 visited strip clubs in Miami and Florida (where Spearmint Rhino has one of its venues) for research purposes.

In GTA 6, Jason and Lucia can both go to strip clubs either together as a couple or individually, and can opt-in for VIP lap dances. As explained in our GTA 6 sex and romance guide , you can throw money at dancers, and if you throw most of your money at one dancer they will remove some of their clothes.

“While gamers across the world immerse themselves in virtual worlds, demand for authentic real-world experiences has never been higher and we’ve had hundreds of inquiries from GTA 6 fans," explained the company president and COO, Kathy Vercher.

"Strip clubs are such an iconic feature in the franchise, and Spearmint Rhino is uniquely positioned to create a real-world experience for gamers. Thanks to the dedication of our Chief Choreographer, Brooke, we’ve been able to bring the in-game lap dance experience into our venues worldwide, with such accuracy that gamers are guaranteed to get a mindblowing real-life experience.”

If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips , Chapter 2 Guide and Tips , and Chapter 3 Guide and Tips . articles.title: Cassette Beasts 2002 Preview: An Unmistakably British – and Impressive – Creature-Collecting RPG
articles.summary: After playing through Cassette Beasts 2002’s opening hours for this preview, I kept playing. While I can’t talk about what I’ve seen since wrapping up the first chunk of my adventure, its opening hours made a strong first impression. I’m charmed by Bytten Studio’s beast design, writing, and distinct take on the creature-collecting RPG. It’s scratching the catch-n-battle itch I get this time of year, and I don’t see that changing anytime soon.
articles.body:
I'm charmed by the beast design, writing, and distinct take on the creature-collecting RPG.

The battle system builds nicely off of what I loved in Pokemon and Persona.

It is unmistakably British in a really fun way.

After playing through Cassette Beasts 2002’s opening hours for this preview, I kept playing. While I can’t talk about what I’ve seen since wrapping up the first chunk of my adventure, its opening hours made a strong first impression. I’m charmed by Bytten Studio’s beast design, writing, and distinct take on the creature-collecting RPG. It’s scratching the catch-n-battle itch I get this time of year, and I don’t see that changing anytime soon.

Lately, I’ve been glued to an online battle simulator from another creature collecting RPG series. Just hopelessly hooked. So when a game like Cassette Beasts gives me an opportunity to stop tugging at the slot machine arm of randomized browser-bound battle teams and build one, I turn my head and pay attention.

Cassette Beasts 2002 made the most of my embattled attention span. Its battle system takes a lot of what I love about Pokemon and Persona and goes a little deeper on some of the ideas that drive the rock-paper-scissors type advantages. For example, water-based attacks will rust metal, weakening metallic Beasts’ defenses. Some attacks might cause Resonance on a metal creature, which automatically knocks it out once enough stacks build up.

I love this approach to type advantages, which capitalizes on strategy in a cool way. The fact that I can just stack Resonance a few times creates a mini-objective in battle that goes beyond just finding the best type advantage. Chasing these objectives adds a lot more depth to this style of turn-based combat that I absolutely adore.

So does the Fusion system, which lets any two Beasts combine into one powerful critter. This is one of the most impressive mechanics I’ve seen in this kind of game. I’m no mathematician, but with over 200 Beasts on the roster (more than 120 are new, by the way), that leaves room for a staggering number of different combinations. While I only saw a small handful of the available Fusions, these super-powered Beasts gain four action points each turn to spend on special moves and abilities in battle, rather than the standard two.

Set in 2000’s London, Cassette Beasts 2002 is unmistakably British. As an American who hasn’t been to the United Kingdom, I’m positive some cultural references and quips have flown over my head, but I still caught a few. For example, the first area in the dream world occupied by the eponymous tape critters (Nodol) is called Bethnal Blue, rather than Bethnal Green.

Naturally, my understanding starts and ends with knowing these names, so I can’t really speak to the actual location or twist Cassette Beasts 2002 is trying to bring to it. Still, that nod to an East London neighborhood feels at home next to references to the works of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle and The Bard. Recent news has me holding out for a Fleming nod.

The world Cassette Beasts 2002 occupies feels as alive as it does tuned to its time and place. Through the course of my demo, I made friends with the locals, bought coffee from the local convenience store worker, and met my exhausted, drink-slinging counterpart across the pond. Brought to life by charming writing and talented voice acting, each character felt believable and interesting enough to actually stop and talk to.

Walking around town reminded me of going outside in my own neighborhood and bumping into a neighbor or bar regular. Maybe this was all canned stuff, designed to fill out and flatter the first part of the game, but the skill trees I saw for some of my digital neighbors suggest otherwise.

Completing sidequests in Nodol, searching in the right places, or progressing in the story will net you Seeds of Inspiration, which you use to fill out the nodes on these NPCs’ skill trees. Each tree represents something different. The shopkeeper’s path gates off helpful items like better healing for your Beasts, whereas my new friend Sai’s skill tree offers upgrades that improve both his skills in battle and helpful upgrades to things like the buffs gained from eating food in-battle.

It would be silly to talk about a game called Cassette Beasts in which you literally record the creatures you’re capturing without mentioning its soundtrack. I heard roughly an EP’s worth of music across the three-hour demo. It’s a small sample size for what’s probably going to be a 20-ish-hour game if the previous Cassette Beasts’ HowLongToBeat page is any indication, but it left a good impression. My favorite stuff showed up in boss fights against foes like Copskin, but the overworld theme for Bethnal Blue was as chill as the snow-capped mountains. I’m sure the best stuff is reserved for late-game boss fights.

Cassette Beasts 2002 promises a nostalgic trip to an era of tape decks and payphones. Built on a clever, distinct battle system that goes beyond just rock, paper, scissors and set in a charming, lived-in world, I’ll probably keep my Steam Deck nearby for a few days to come. It’s slated for release in March of next year, so it’ll be a while before you can get your hands on this one. But it’s just as well; you’re probably going to be pretty busy with another game in which the soundtrack is heavily emphasized for the next few months.

While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!

articles.title: GTA 6: Here's Why You Should Go Back to Jason's House After Chapter 1
articles.summary: Here’s why you should go back to Jason’s house after chapter 1 of GTA 6.
articles.body:
Warning: spoilers for Chapter 1 of GTA 6 follow.

If you’ve played through chapter one of GTA 6, you’ll know that Jason’s home isn’t in the best of shape following its final mission. On fire, and certainly no place to raise a child, the crib, coffee table, and all of your chosen home improvements are left either shattered or cindered by the time Lucia escapes, taking with her only one valuable: a photo of the couple’s son, Tomás. But not all is lost, and it’s worth going back to check what remains.

From the beginning of chapter two onward, going back to Jason’s waterside house can be a risky move to make. Flick open the map, and you’ll see a red area surrounding his immediate neighbourhood that signifies a police presence in the area. Of course, you’re free to head back straight away, but you’ll see a few cop cars sat outside his home, with a few people waiting in case you do return to the scene of the crime. Sneak past them if you trust your stealth skills, or opt for a much quicker and violent smash-and-grab maneuver if that’s more your style.

If you're patient, though, that heat will eventually diminish over the course of the story, so you can walk straight through the front door. I’m not exactly sure if that’s tied to your progress through GTA 6’s main missions, or the in-game clock itself, but I can confirm that from around halfway through chapter three, that red zone had disappeared for me.

Once inside the ashen remains of Jason’s former quiet life, there are a couple of items of note to grab hold of. Both of these can be found under the floorboards of the bedroom where Jason’s stash once lay hidden. While you won’t be able to recover all of the money you stored there before realising it would be gone forever — I guess it burned, whereas the metal tin next to it protected its contents — you can find both his personal collection of photos and a rainy day fund worth $5,000.

The former is a nice extra wrinkle to the story, as Jason and Lucia will make sure to cherish these photos, alongside the one she recovered of Tommy, and carry them with them from home to home around Leonida on their nomadic adventures. The latter is no small amount when starting again from scratch at the outset of chapter two, which does make the risk of getting busted worth it to get a head start in Port Gellhorn. Wait until chapter three, as I did, and that amount of money makes less of a difference.

But that isn’t all. When Lucia grapples with the two masked men who set the home on fire, Jason’s pet snake, Dolores, makes a daring escape when her glass enclosure is smashed. We saw her head for the door, but are left wondering whether she managed to dance through the flames to safety. Well, when returning to the home, make sure to check under the back steps, where you can find our serpentine friend alive and well. And she’s not alone either. Get a closer look to find her curled up around some eggs, signalling a whole host of mini Dolores’s are on the way. Perhaps they’ll rebuild this home together, and turn the whole of Key Lento into a snake town over time. Far-fetched, perhaps, but have you seen some of the bonkers sh*t happening in this game?

It’s just one example of how Rockstar has managed to build out the world of GTA 6 so successfully, making it feel like a place that carries on living even when you’re not there. This sort of thing is littered throughout Leonida as you progress through the story and the passing of time takes effect. Road and building works that start out as mounds of dirt slowly become more developed as chapters go by, with pipes being laid down and bricks stacked.

And Jason’s house isn’t the only place he and Lucia call home that’s worth revisiting long after they’ve departed. The Startlet Motel from chapter two also changes, offering new gameplay and story opportunities. GTA 6 is a game that rewards curiosity, often answering your questions with a satisfying answer, and returning to Jason’s home is just one example of it.

articles.summary: Longtime director of The Hunger Games franchise Francis Lawrence has revealed that all five films he has directed in the series were initially rated R and opened up about the process of making them PG-13.
articles.body:
Longtime director of The Hunger Games franchise Francis Lawrence has revealed that all five films he directed in the series were initially rated R, prompting clever workarounds when editing them.

On paper, The Hunger Games franchise is tonally very interesting. Although it's a young adult novel series, targeting teenagers, it's about children being forced to fight to the death in a dystopian society. The books don't hold back on the violence, and the films have always had to walk a fine line so they can reach the widest audience possible. The process of making the movies PG-13 is complicated and often inconsistent.

When speaking with Kevin McCarthy , director Francis Lawrence noted that all five of the Hunger Games films he has worked on were initially rated R. The director noted that across his whole career, he has run into an issue of making a movie with a PG-13 rating in mind, but the MPA (Motion Picture Association) reserves the right to give it an R if it's too "intense," even if there's no excessive blood, gore, language, or nudity. It happened with Constantine, it was a concern with I Am Legend, and it has happened regularly with The Hunger Games series.

In one of the Mockingjay films, Lawrence had to cut a scene of a little girl crying and screaming over the body of her dead mother. There wasn't any blood, but the performance was so visceral that it pushed the film closer to an R-rating.

He revealed that the process is somewhat subjective, as the people who rate the movies change, their tastes change, and he was even able to identify specific changes on particular movies.

In regards to Sunrise on the Reaping, he believes that the MPA has become more "conservative" with their judgment of a film, prompting them to tweak the project and show it to the organization four or five times. He also said that sometimes he makes the content more intense on purpose when presenting it to the MPA, so when they edit it, they can show the "intended" version, and it looks more tame by comparison. One example of this is amplifying sound effects to make it sound gnarlier, and then reigning it in on subsequent edits.

Lawrence went on to note that he is surprised by how much these movies can get away with in a PG-13 context, but believes there's a thematic relevance that the MPA accepts.

"It does help that there's been so many of these now that there's [a] precedent," he said. "There's also real thematic relevance to these stories, and I think that also really helps, that in the end they're anti-violence stories. They're about the consequences of violence, the consequences of war; they're really about themes that are educating people. I do think the MPA takes that into consideration when they look at sequences that are intense. They have different emotional values, and it's not really splattercore, in a way.

"But I definitely do intensify beyond a limit of where I think it will be accepted as PG-13 purposely, because I know we are going to have to pull back on certain things."

He explained that certain deaths were more brutal and gratuitous in initial cuts of the film, but ultimately had to be adjusted for a PG-13 rating.

"One thing I really wanted to keep was we had a very specific neck wound on Maysilee in her death. Basically the one that kills her is right here," said Lawrence while pointing at the center of his neck. "And he's covering it and when his hand comes off, you can see blood starting to drip out of it, and you can see the hole, and it's why she can't speak. And they made us get rid of that, and that's what killed me."

The Hunger Games films are far from the only big mainstream action movies that have to get creative with how they depict violence. Crew members on The Dark Knight were confident the film would be rated R, despite Christopher Nolan and the studio working to avoid that. They were able to get around a harder rating thanks to the fact the film does most of the gorier acts of violence off-screen or even playing it off as a joke.

"It’s kind of shocking that The Dark Knight ended up being PG-13," said the film's cinematographer Wally Pfister in a 2018 interview . "All of Chris’s movies would be PG-13 to open it up to a wider audience. Somehow, he always had some magic with the MPA.

"Lo and behold, he has the pencil and I’m like, 'You are not getting the PG-13 with that. There’s no way this is going in. He’s driving this pencil through a guy’s head!' And I was wrong. Chris was always right, whether you liked it or not. You’d be like, 'F*** you, you were right again.' With this pencil trick, I thought, ‘If it has the right amount of levity, we’ll sell this and it won’t come off as being violent but it’ll come off as being a magic trick and it’ll come off as being a punchline.’ And it was!"

Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now.

articles.title: We Build LEGO Godzilla, Who Will Tower Over Your Other LEGO Models
articles.body:
For Black Friday 2026 , LEGO is launching a massive model of Godzilla, King of the Monsters. It is a LEGO Ideas model, which means it began its life as a fan design by Matthew Esposito . He received the requisite votes for official LEGO approval, and he will also share in the profits.

This is a bulky build that looks more impressive in person than it does on its box cover. It comes with two interchangeable mouth insertions: either a large tongue or an Atomic Heat Ray, the latter of which extends his height to over two feet tall. Space concerns aside, the choice seems clear if you're putting this city stomper on display.

Godzilla fans should know this model is based upon the ongoing ' Monsterverse ' iteration of the creature, which began with Godzilla (2014). Monsterverse is an American franchise, not to be confused with the original Japanese Toho franchise, which released its 34th film ( Godzilla Minus Zero ) this November.

But artists have redesigned Godzilla many times, including from movie to movie. So even though it might not be the exact Godzilla you love the most, this LEGO model is immediately recognizable as the icon, because it has the general characteristics that most iterations share in common: the pear-shaped body, the comparatively smaller dinosaur head, and the dorsal fins that line its back. The model's main inspiration is the Godzilla from Godzilla: King of the Monsters (2019), but even so, it's a bit sleeker and thinner than that one. So it might be best to think about this as yet another monster design alongside the others – loyal to the design ethos, but unique in its approach.

LEGO Godzilla comes in a large box, which encases two smaller boxes. Each smaller box contains approximately 20 bags. Added together, it's 41 bags in all, plus three instruction booklets. There are no stickers and no printed tiles.

You build one leg, then the pelvis, and then the other leg. You connect both legs to the pelvis with durable ball joints, and stand it up. To give you an idea of how bottom-heavy Godzilla is: Just the legs and pelvis comprise half of the entire build. And even so, LEGO made clever design choices to accentuate his bulk. Take the armor plating on his lower legs, for example. They hang off a hinge near the ankle, which creates the illusion of a thicker, more substantial leg, even though it's mostly air with no bricks to fill it out.

Then you focus on the tail, which you build in segments. Connecting them all creates a sense of accomplishment, because most large LEGO builds (including this one) take shape through layering, first by building the Technic skeleton underneath and then building the musculature and skin via plating. But with the tail, you're seeing the entire appendage take form in front of you, immediately, and it's easy to see where it begins and where it will eventually end.

Each tail segment contains dorsal fin elements. You need to either build directly onto the tail piece or clip a larger fin to it, which adds a varied, visual touch. The tail drags along the ground, and the instructions let you decide whether it will rest on the left side or the right side of the creature. You then turn to the correct page (sort of like a Choose-Your-Own-Adventure book) and proceed.

The third and final instruction booklet shows you how to build the arms, the head, and some final, large dorsal fins on the creature's back. These are the fussiest parts of the build, owing to their smaller size and weaker connection points. But when everything is complete, the final result is very intimidating. Ironically, the smaller head and arms only emphasize how large the rest of the creature is. Godzilla's skin cleverly appropriates the LEGO bricks' pips as rough texture.

This is a wonderful model, and we recommend it with one important reservation; it is best displayed from a side profile angle only, with its head pointed upwards. Any other angle or posture, and the model looks odd and ungainly.

I think the reason for this one-dimensionality – for favoring one possible display angle over the others – is the developers were trying to nail a single, iconic Godzilla pose. It's this one from the promotional poster for Godzilla: King of the Monsters, in which Godzilla is looking up, shooting his atomic heat ray directly towards the heavens:

And to be fair, this model nails that pose very, very well, and it looks exactly like the poster. But that comes at the sacrifice of other possible poses. Take the neck, for example. To ensure that the head can tilt up convincingly, the designers included extra grey bricks around the neck to hide the seams. That's a great thing, but only for that specific pose. Those extra bricks limit Godzilla's movement, and he can only point his head up, diagonally up, or straight across. He can't, for example, look down, which is a problem if you want to pose him looking down at the city or humans he's about to destroy.

It's not a problem isolated to the neck either; the back is also ramrod straight and does not allow Godzilla to adjust himself down or forward. Again, that's fantastic for that one pose . But it doesn't serve Godzilla well for any other, alternative setup.

Normally, this sort of one-notedness, especially in adult sets, wouldn't be that big of a deal, because an adult set doesn't need to be a malleable plaything. But because so much of our popular concept of Godzilla has him looking down at things rather than up at them, it's especially noticeable.

Surely, a creative builder can modify the current set for more flexibility. And then, LEGO Godzilla can look down as he stomps some LEGO Ninjago cities, while minifigures scream and scramble for dear life.

LEGO Godzilla (Set #21375) retails for $449.99 and includes 5363 pieces. It will be available beginning on Black Friday, November 27.

Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 still receives significant support two years after launch. We’re now up to patch 16.0, which makes significant balance changes to the game.

In terms of new features, we’ve got a major expansion of the Vanguard class’ combat abilities (the Grapnel Launcher can now be used at close range!), the new Revenge status effect (hitting enemies afflicted with Revenge also deals damage to nearby enemies), and Wargear 2.3 (Bulwark can now equip and customize Cloak!).

As for cosmetics, the hotly anticipated Deathwatch Champion Pack is out now as part of the Season Pass. There’s also a Mortifactors Cosmetic Pack. I’ve put the balance changes as part of the patch notes below, if you want to skip to them to see what’s happened to your class.

Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 Patch 16 Screenshots

Also interesting is the note about tech improvements with patch 16. Publisher Focus Entertainment says loading times have improved, which players will welcome. There are also memory optimizations, “minor” performance improvements, and “general” connectivity improvements. Anyone who’s played or is still playing Space Marine 2 will hope these improvements are meaningful.

Focus has said that next year, Space Marine 2 will receive three more updates until its third anniversary. Patch 17, 18 and 19 will offer free content as well as Season Pass 3 content with the cosmetic DLCs. There’s a lot of excitement around Patch 17, which adds a brand-new class, the Apothecary , complete with its signature Absolvor Bolt Pistol. Patch 17 also adds a new Operation and fresh Heroic weapons, and a rework of the Heavy class. A new Imperial Fist Champion Pack and a Cosmetic Pack for the Minotaurs chapter are also on the way.

The Nova Pro is first and foremost a gaming headset, and it delivers big sound with its big 40mm neodymium dynamic drivers and 360° spatial sound effects (via SteelSeries Sonar for PC, Tempest 3D Audio for PS5, and Microsoft Spatial Sound for Xbox). articles.title: GTA 6 Weather Still Not Varied Even After the Patch? PS5 Players Are Sharing a Method That May Help Rain and Thunderstorms Kick In
articles.summary: Rockstar recently dropped the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 which, among other things, included a fix for the game’s lack of weather variety. Some players were left still experiencing issues, but now there’s seemingly a workaround for PS5 players specifically.
articles.body:
Rockstar recently dropped the first post-launch patch for GTA 6 which, among other things, included a fix for the game’s lack of weather variety. Some players were left still experiencing issues, but now there’s seemingly a workaround for PS5 players specifically.

Lack of weather variety was something I noticed myself during the game’s review period, but Rockstar deployed a small fix during that time too. It was hard to tell whether it was working as intended because the weather also grows more stark as you move through the game.

“The weather types change throughout each day, and the overall weather pattern changes per chapter, evolving from generally very good weather in the first chapter to much more changeable and stormy in the last chapter,” said Owen Shepherd, vice president of art: lighting and rendering at Rockstar, when I asked.

“This is analogous to Florida’s weather patterns in winter through to summer autumn. During the first chapters there are pockets of rain but due to the localization of weather it is possible to miss these."

However, it seems like the issue persisted into the live version of the game, blurring the line between thematically appropriate and accurate weather patterns and unintended bug. The latest patch fixed this for the most part, but some players found they were still experiencing minimal weather changes.

If you’re having the same issue, there might be a fix (discovered by X / Twitter user @mauricioce85796 ). On PS5, you need to turn off your console and boot it into safe mode by holding the power button down until it beeps.

From there, choose option six and select “clear system cache.” According to people who have tested it, this forces the patch to do its job.

“I have 56 hours in this game so far and I haven’t experienced any dramatic weather,” said Rockstar fan account Gameroll . “I did this and upon loading I was IMMEDIATELY met with this storm. I’m delighted.”

Of course, this could be a placebo, but players in the replies have been trying it and immediately seeing results. “Guys, I can confirm, it’s working,” said one happy X / Twitter user who showcased a rainy clip. “Can confirm, weather is more varied!” said another .

Clearing your cache on PS5 won’t delete game saves or installed games. It just deletes temporary system files and lets the console recreate fresh ones without erasing your games, saved data, screenshots, or account settings. It helps resolve system feature glitches, slow performance, stuttering, app or game launch errors, and network or sync hiccups. People have been doing it for years, claiming to see performance benefits as a result.

articles.body:
Whether you're looking for the TV with the best image quality and you've got money to spend, or you've got a tight budget and value is paramount, Black Friday has got you covered. If you're planning to upgrade to OLED this year, you'll find a deal for it. If you're looking for something bigger, like a 75" or dare I say 100", you'll find a deal for that too.

65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED Smart TV (2026)

65" Samsung M80H 4K Mini LED Smart TV (2026)

65" TCL QM8L 4K SQD-Mini LED QLED Google TV (2026)

55" Hisense U7 Mini-LED ULED 4K Fire TV (2026)

50" Vizio VQM50C-10 4K QD Mini LED Smart TV

If you're looking for an affordable TV that offers solid image quality, the Hisense QD5 is hard to beat. For Black Friday, you can pick up a 55" model for under $200 or a 75" model for under $400. This 2026 Hisense TV offers great image quality that punches above its weight class thanks to Hisense's proprietary Hi-QLED panel with direct-lit LED backlighting. The QD5 officially supports a number of HDR formats including HDR10, Dolby Vision, and HLG. Roku smart interface is also integrated, which is considered one of the best built-in smart interfaces you can get from a budget TV. It's definitely a favorite of mine; I prefer it over Google TV and Fire TV.

The Best Black Friday Budget Samsung TV Deal

Not everyone feels comfortable buying a TV brand that isn't Samsung, LG, or Sony (although, technically, Sony TVs are now made by TCL). In that case, the best budget TV deal from one of these brands is easily the Samsung M80H TV . This is a new 2026 model TV that features a mini LED panel and a native 144Hz refresh rate so you can play supported PlayStation 5, Xbox, and PC games at up to 144fps. The 65" TV is currently less than $500 and you can't find many (any?) TVs in that price range that offer this level of features and a Samsung/LG/Sony brand name.

LG's most popular OLED TV is on sale for Black Friday. Amazon currently has the 65" LG Evo C6 4K OLED TV for $1,349.99 with free delivery. To be perfectly honest, I think this is a rather lukewarm Black Friday price for LG's current model C-series OLED TV. There's a possibility that if you wait a couple of days, a better deal will drop. That said, this is the lowest straight-up price I've seen so far this year by $50.

The C6 is LG's current 2026 model in the LG's C-series OLED TV lineup. LG's C-series OLED TV in general has been our favorite TVs for console gaming for many years thanks to its outstanding image quality, low input lag, and high refresh rate. This is one of the best TVs you can get for streaming 4K HDR content in its intended glory. It boasts the near-infinite black levels, near-infinite contrast ratio, and near-instantaneous response times you'd expect from any OLED TV. The C6 is also equipped with modern gaming features including a native 120Hz panel that can be pushed to as high as 165Hz, HDMI 2.1 inputs, variable refresh rate and auto low latency mode.

The Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV Gives OLED a Run for Its Money

Last year, Hisense pioneered the first RGB Mini-LED TV with its 116UX model. Granted it was only available as a massive 116" screen that retailed for $20,000. In 2026, Hisense released its second generation RGB Mini-LED tech at a much more affordable price point with its UR-series lineup. For Black Friday, you can get it for even less. Best Buy has just discounted the 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV from $2,000 all the way down to $899.99 and the 75" model from $2,500 down to $1399.99, both with free delivery. These are the lowest prices since launch and beats previous lows by $200.

RGB Mini-LED is an evolution of Mini-LED technology. Traditional mini-LED TVs consist of an array of blue LED that are passed through RGB filters to produced the desired color. RGB Mini-LED TVs use red, green, and blue LEDs instead of just blue, which means the pixels no longer need filters to produce the desired color. The result is more accurate color reproduction, less blooming and, most importantly, a wider color gamut. Color gamut of RGB Mini-LED surpasses that of OLEDs, since current-generation OLEDs also use color filters combined with blue OLEDs. How does that translate in the real world? It means that you see richer, more accurate colors, smoother gradients and less banding than even OLEDs.

TCL introduces its own SQD mini LED tech in the QM8L TV

One of the best new TVs of 2026 dropped to its lowest price ever ahead of Black Friday. The QM8L is a pretty significant upgrade over last year's QM8K model thanks to the introduction of TCL's highly-touted SQD technology. SQD - which stands for Super Quantum Dot - is a more refined version of QLED tech. Quantum dot panels have a layer of microscopic crystals measuring a few nanometers in size that are able to separate light into precise colors. SQD tech uses even smaller crystals - as small as a single nanometer in width. This allows SQD panels to pack in even more dimming zones, usually numbering in the thousands, which in turn produces a brighter image with higher contrast and richer colors.
