articles.title: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth Director David Fincher Sparks Backlash for 'Wildly Dystopian' Vision of AI-powered Filmmaking
articles.summary: Director David Fincher has sparked a backlash after setting out what some have called a “dystopian” vision for AI-fueled filmmaking, amid controversy over AI use in Netflix movie The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth.
articles.body:
Director David Fincher has sparked a backlash after setting out what some have called a “dystopian” vision for AI-fueled filmmaking, amid controversy over AI use in Netflix movie The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth .

Fincher, who directed Seven, Fight Club, and The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, has reunited with long-term collaborator Brad Pitt for The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, which was written by Quentin Tarantino. It is a standalone sequel and spinoff to Tarantino’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood, with Pitt reprising his role as stunt double Cliff Booth.

In a recent interview with Sean Fennessey on The Ringer’s Big Picture podcast , Fincher confirmed that he used AI to sync the best take of a line reading with the best performance take when they didn’t align on camera, in order to speed up production by cutting down the number of takes needed. Essentially, he used AI to replace dialogue and adjust actors’ lip movements in post-production.

“We could use AI to re-lip that thing,” he said. “So it was freeing, it was the freeing up of… think of this entirely plastically. We’re not chiseling this out of marble. We’re working with plasticine. You know what I mean? Just giving ourselves that freedom to go, ‘what is the best thing on the eye, and then what is the best thing on the ear,’ and f***ing do not worry about how we’re going to get there, because we will figure out a way. And we did, in most cases. I think there’s a couple of shots [that] didn’t quite work, but they’re getting there. By the time it’s on service.”

Fincher added that the actors spent just a handful of days re-recording dialogue. Dialogue replacement was just 5% conventionally done, the rest “all AI.”

But it was his comments made later in the interview, where Fincher described how he sees directing with AI going in the future, that have sparked the most vociferous response.

“I’m imagining — and what I’ve seen with AI technology — I’m imagining a world in the next year where everything that humans do great, like sculpting, painting, ageing, blowing fake spider’s webs into the corner, smoking up a volume, putting a shaft of light in it, putting a crazy f***ing wig on somebody, doing all their makeup… like, I can imagine a world where — and I don’t think we’re far away — you hire all the same people. And you walk into a set that’s beautifully handcrafted, and you hire all those people, and you shoot the master. You shoot the master 20, 25 times till you get it worked out exactly. And you’re doing surface capture at the exact same time that you’re filming. And then you go in and you sit all the actors in chairs wherever they land, and they perform from the clavicles up, same scene, but you move the crew. The crew’s now moving to the next stage, they’re pre-lighting that, they’re getting that ready.

“So essentially, the filmmaking process is about just shooting the masters. And all of the iteration, the over-shoulders, the close-ups, all that stuff is derived from the material that you do sitting in a chair after everyone leaves.

“And then, the part that seems to provoke such a violent, vitriolic response in people — ‘Oh my God, he made me do it 20 times!’ — it’s like, now I don’t need to do that, because I won’t miss focus in AI. And I will land a stick the dolly shot in AI. And I will be able to make sure that that hair doesn’t cross right in front of your cornea in AI.

“And it’ll still be based on real human beings, and it’ll still be based on real human — the way humans move and how they traverse a set and however they pull up their trousers before they sit down or take their coat off — all that stuff will be there, but people will only have to do it 15 times.”

In the interview, Fennessey then asked: “Does working that way appeal to you?”

The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth Images

Fincher’s comments were roundly criticized on social media, where people hit out at not just the heavy use of AI in The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth, but the prospect of seeing a performance from the likes of Brad Pitt that isn’t real.

“David Lynch: The camera accidentally caught a crew member in the mirror so I incorporated him into the story and ended up with one of the most memorable characters in TV and movie history,” writer and critic David Hering said in a post on social media . “David Fincher: I spent $400m to change the shape of Brad Pitt’s mouth when he says ‘hello.’”

“Any movie that uses even a sliver of AI should be immediately disqualified from awards consideration,” said another person . “Disgusting.”

“Saying, ‘I wanna take an actor’s eye movement from Take 1 with an actors lip movement from Take 3’…that’s not the performance the actor gave on set! You don’t get to create the perfect performance by Frankenstein-ing a ‘perfect version’ of the performance and call it directing,” actor Mike Kalinowski commented .

“I’m not saying Fincher is not an incredible director. But he’s also known for doing an ungodly amount of takes to get exactly what he wants. But you’re when you’re working with actors, it’s never gonna be perfect. That’s what makes it art.”

One person called Fincher’s proposed production process “wildly dystopian,” another “depressing as f**k.” Another quipped: “there is no longer a need for David Fincher.” "Imagine doing 135 takes just to be asked back for an ADR session where the Ben Grokfleck Machine updates your lips," another said .

“Fincher's vision of a largely A.I. production is undeniably bleak but I suspect people would be less perplexed if it was more widely understood (as a friend remarked to me recently) that Fincher's filmmaking process was always more about control than perfection,” writer Brendan Hodges said .

However, there are some that are defending Fincher here, saying his AI vision isn’t a million miles away from the editing process that goes on without AI, where different parts of takes are edited together to create the best scene. The counter to that response is of course that there’s a difference between editing together actual performance from different takes, and using AI to create a performance that was never given.

AI is one of, if not the hottest topics in the entertainment industry, and Hollywood is currently wrestling with maintaining its humanity in the creative process while cutting down costs and raising productivity. Hollywood, like the video game industry, is beset with layoffs as cost-cutting and AI disruption hit hard.

Earlier this month, Star Wars writer Tony Gilroy sounded the alarm over the rising tide of AI slop that he said was a threat to human-made movies. Speaking to Vanity Fair , Gilroy implored movie fans to vote against the spread of AI data centers — and even jokingly suggested that the artificial intelligence-fuelling tech hubs should be blown up.

In September, acclaimed filmmaker Guillermo Del Toro spoke out against AI , saying the “alchemy” of creativity and discovery humans experience when crafting a story or artwork is unachievable by a machine, and that many of the best works are often elevated by "accidents" that happen during the creative process.

The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth opened in IMAX theaters on November 25, and hits Netflix on December 23.

Photo by Tristan Fewings/Getty Images for BFI.

articles.title: The Rings of Power Season 3 Ending Explained With Showrunners J. D. Payne and Patrick McKay
articles.summary: The Rings of Power Season 3  just ended, so showrunners J. D. Payne and Patrick McKay break down everything that happened - and what to expect next.
articles.body:
Spoilers follow for The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3.

The last frame of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 focuses on Sauron (Charlie Vickers) looking straight to camera as he bows before the crowing King Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle) and the very sober-looking elves Galadriel (Morfydd Clark), Celeborn (Jamie Campbell Bower) and Gil-galad (Benjamin Walker). A slight smirk has never been more dangerous.

With the fourth season of The Rings of Power confirmed, series creators and showrunners J. D. Payne and Patrick McKay spoke with IGN to preview what’s coming in Season 4 and beyond. From the Galadriel/Celeborn/Sauron triangle to Queen Miriel’s (Cynthia Addai-Robinson) sacrifices that seem for naught to Gandalf’s future trials and beyond, the two break down how Middle-earth will fare in the planned last two seasons.

The Rings of Power: Season 3 Ending Explained

Payne told IGN that they settled on Sauron’s last look for the season early on, despite mulling whether they should close on the forging of the One Ring instead. “There was maybe a half a second where we said, ‘Gosh, the forging of the ring is such a climactic moment. Should we end the season there and then let all the next season be about Númenór?’” he said. “Very quickly we were like, ‘No, no, no!’ You want to actually give all the other storylines a chance to coalesce. You had Gandalf out in the east working to try to take the Dark Wizard either off the field or onto his side. And Númenór in the west are figuring out their civil war and Pharazôn and Miriel's marriage. We felt like if we ended on the forging of the ring, you would feel a little frustrated.”

McKay added that they wanted to downplay this finale after two seasons of massive, action-centric season endings. “We wanted a season that was tighter, tauter, more psychological,” he explained. “And we have this great moment from mythology – that Sauron surrendered with a plan of a longer game.

“Now, that's scary as showrunners making a show in 2026,” McKay admitted. “Are people going to be like, ‘Wait, what ?’ I think that's still scary. Reactions are just coming in right now. But we also felt that it was bold, and we hadn't seen it before. When we were really [story-]beating out the very ending of the season, Sauron falls to his knees in front of the army — that image felt so strong. We were just like, ‘Let's stop right there and leave them hanging.’ It felt like a satisfying ending.”

A huge event in the Second Age of Middle-earth is the Fall of Númenór to Sauron, and McKay and Payne confirm that that train is now on the tracks.

“It’s a real opportunity to show a civilizational decline,” Payne said of what’s to come. “Fall is one of Tolkien's recurring themes [that] he goes back to again and again. We've already seen the cracks in Númenór. We know they're there, so how do you exploit those to get the mightiest empire of men that has ever existed and totally take them off the map?”

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 Photos

Without spoiling, Payne said they’re very excited to show it in a “multifaceted way,” along with its effect on many different characters and storylines. But there’s also the interpersonal drama to come between Pharazôn and Sauron. In prior seasons, audiences have already seen the Dark Lord pick apart Galadriel and others, so how will Pharazôn be undone?

“Pharazôn is a very skilled and savvy manipulator in his own right,” Payne said of the King. “He's a massive politician. He's one who is always looking seven moves down the chessboard and trying to figure out how to outsmart his adversary. When you get two snakes in a barrel, each one trying to outmaneuver the other one and look ahead, how is Sauron able to concoct a lose-lose scenario that even someone as savvy as Pharazôn might fall prey to?”

McKay was also gleeful about it. “The idea of putting Charlie Vickers and Trystan Gravelle on a collision course — that's a potent mix. Those are two very exciting actors with very different approaches, playing very different kinds of characters. We're pretty excited.”

Also in that Númenórean psychological soup is the sacrificial Queen Miriel, who only married Pharazôn to join his army with her Faithful in order to bring down Sauron. And now the Dark Lord is coming home with them?

“It is a terrible compromise she has made, but one that she believes is the best given everything on her plate,” McKay pointed out. “She's trying to save her people and save the world, and she's sacrificing herself in the process. Now extrapolate – what does that person do when Sauron's here with the influence he's having? There's two things that person could do. They could continue doubling down and trying to fix it, digging the hole even deeper to protect her people. Or she could say, ‘I'm out.’ I think if you look at Cynthia's amazing performance and the journey this character has been on, it's going to be a rough road ahead for the Queen. The Queen has a big story next season. Everyone in Númenór does.”

In Season 1, Sauron/Halbrand really created a connection with Galadriel, and his betrayal has continued to pull on both of them through Season 3. With the return of the long-lost Celeborn this season, a choice was made. In the finale, the married elves chose one another, but Sauron was clearly looking right at Galadriel when he took the knee for Pharazôn.

McKay said it was their intention to tell a real, messy love story this season with Galadriel and Celeborn, with an eye to countering Sauron’s quest to forge the ring. “When [Galadriel and Celeborn] see each other, on the one hand, they're both in tears. But also, it's like, ‘What does this mean?’ They're unmoored. It breaks their reality.

“By the end of the season, they have renegotiated their marriage and found a place where they can be equals … both of them have been traumatized by the Dark Lord,” McKay points out. “That also means that that core relationship and the dream they had of the realm and bringing light and beauty into the world – they're going to fight and try to protect that ever more fiercely now that they really know the stakes of it.”

As for Sauron, Payne said that there are many prices he must pay for his mission to take Middle-earth, including how he feels about Galadriel. “We know that this is going to be a connection that endures into the Third Age,” he said of Tolkien’s lore. “Galadriel tells us that she knows the Dark Lord and his mind, and that ever does he grope after her to know hers. So Sauron is never letting this go. But she says, ‘Still the way is shut.’ She has closed that door, and now we're going to watch as she figures out a way to heal from the damage that it has done to her. And Celeborn finds a way to heal from the damage that it has also done to him.”

McKay said how they will achieve that ties to Pharazôn asking for their counsel about how to get at Sauron before the battle that never happened. “That speaks to the role of Galadriel and Celeborn moving forward, which is — they know this guy,” he pointed out. “They know him better than anyone, which makes them natural adversaries for him, so that will come back around as well.”

What about the fledgling wizard who succeeded in helping the Dark Wizard / Pallando (Ciarán Hinds) redeem his evil ways? Gandalf has his staff and his hat, and that huge win under his belt. Who does he help next?

Payne teased that Gandalf’s work is far from done, and instead of turning one heart, he’s going to have to figure out how to turn the “hearts of entire people and leaders.”

“What are the challenges that come together when he has to get people who are enemies, or deep enemies, to put aside differences [and] come together?” Payne posed. “What sacrifices will he have to make? These are all things that are still down the road for Gandalf.”

The End Is Nigh and They Know Their Ending

McKay said they are now in the phase of shaping this series where they’re dovetailing back into the concrete canon of Tolkien’s books, and adaptation going forward will be more precise.

“From the very beginning when we first started our first writers' room, it was about charting those giant moments,” he explained. “In some ways, the making of the three rings was the end of the first season. The seven and the nine [rings were] in the second [season]. And this season was all about the One Ring, ending in [Sauron’s] surrender. And there's a very clear plan for the rest. We know where we're heading.

“We even know what the last shot is,” he revealed. “There is some problem-solving we have yet to do, like how much of this? Or, how are we going to do that? But the garden of forking paths is narrow ahead. We know what we're doing next [season], and I think we have a pretty good idea what we're going to do the time after that. It does feel like we're over the hump, and it does feel like the destination is in sight.”

articles.title: GTA 6's Cartel Heist Might Be Rockstar's Best Ever Mission, But Only If You Do It Badly
articles.summary: GTA 6's chapter three heist might be Rockstar's best ever mission, but only if you do it badly.
articles.body:
Warning: This article contains spoilers for chapter three of GTA 6.

Chapter 3 of GTA 6 ends with a bang. It’s arguably Rockstar’s greatest ever mission and a culmination of every bank job the developer has designed since GTA 4’s Three Leaf Clover burst onto the scene. A daring raid on the Sinfrontera National Bank in downtown Vice City, what starts out as a slick operation quickly goes haywire, resulting in shootouts with armored police, helicopters chasing a bus that has had the roof ripped off, and the death of one of your gang members.

The funny thing is, you may be reading that and thinking that’s not what happened to you at all. That’s because the back half of The Cartel Heist can go in wildly different directions. You can do it much more cleanly, but it’s nowhere near as fun. Sorry, Nicole.

A lot has to go in your favour to execute the perfect heist. Making sure you correctly prep is key, meaning you’ll have to extract all of the info possible out of Monty when he’s dangling over reptilian teeth, protect Pete’s shipment of weapons correctly, and plant enough explosives on the cell towers. Then there’s also everything you have to get going your way inside the mission itself, which is mainly tied to not wasting time and nailing the vault minigame. You can get the full details on everything you’ll need to do, step-by-step, on our excellent guides page .

Nail it, and your getaway driver will turn up as planned by the underground entrance; you’ll load up the truck with stacks of cash and simply drive off undetected. There are obvious benefits to doing this. Not only is there the satisfaction of pulling off such a complex job cleanly, but you’ll earn $150,000 from it, rather than the $100,000 you’d otherwise get, plus Nicole, your charming safecracking tutor, will survive. What you will miss out on, though, is one of Rockstar’s finest blockbuster sequences.

The path truly branches once you leave the bank’s vault, but in all truth, your fate has likely been long sealed by that point. You’ll have needed to keep a keen eye on your time in the bottom right corner and have made sure all ten bundles of bills have been secured by the time the alarm goes off and all hell breaks loose. That’s when things kick up a notch, and legions of Vice City police and NOOSE enforcers turn up at the front doors. A lobby shootout commences, with enemies turning up from all directions in an effort to stop you from leaving with your haul. It's a fantastic encounter that borders on sensory overload thanks to the rattle of gunfire, thick smoke, and blaring alarms.

The slick transitions between characters only add to the sense of cinema, with Lucia throwing a smoke grenade launcher up to the balcony for Jason to catch, punctuated by a highly satisfying second or two of slow motion. This elegantly moves the action onto the streets, allowing you to get a glimpse of the full challenge awaiting you and your gang outside. Michael Mann’s Heat has long been an influence on Grand Theft Auto, but never has the sensation of watching the movie’s signature heist been replicated as well as it has here. It makes Three Leaf Clover firmly look like the first draft that it was back in 2008.

As the fight moves outdoors, Raul’s backup plan comes to fruition with Karim arriving behind the wheel of a public bus. Up to this point in GTA 6’s story, the heist leader has remained a mysterious presence, slinking in and out of scenes with an undeniable air of cool. It’s not until now, though, that we get to see him in full flow, leading with calm authority. He’s quickly become one of my favourite characters across the whole Grand Theft Auto series — embodying the swagger and ruthless execution of a lusciously long-maned Danny Ocean.

Of course, it would all be too simple for everyone to walk onto the bus and drive off into the sunset. Lucia, Raul, Andrea, and Karim all make it on board, but have to make the tough decision to leave without Jason and Nicole. Having to find an alternative escape route, it calls on Jason to flex all of his military muscles and escort Nicole to safety. Bleeding out thanks to a gunshot to the stomach, she makes it to a SWAT van that Jason takes the wheel of. The chase is on.

GTA 6’s big-scale missions are when the dynamic player-switching really comes into its own. Before we know it, we’re back on the bus and having to hold off cars, trucks, and helicopters as Lucia from the back seat. Nothing can prevent the roof from being torn off by some hooks from a nearby truck, though, in what might be the whole mission’s most jaw-dropping moment. It’s just pure flexing from Rockstar at this point, and I’m all for it. Not only does it add to the spectacle, but it makes you rethink how to take down your pursuers due to your cover being violently rearranged.

All of that prep work you did on previous missions may not have led to you getting the perfect heist escape, but it still has its benefits here. Manage to protect all of the weapons cargo provided by Pete? You’ll get a very fun grenade launcher to wield here and blow away the opposition with. The number of variables within this mission is staggering, and a real showcase of how the little choices you make as Jason and Lucia affect their story. The whole of chapter three has been building up to this moment, and knowing that every step before it actually meant something makes it all the more rewarding.

One final character switch is then made, with Jason tasked with catching up with the bus and getting both him and Nicole on board. Sadly, no matter what you do, once everyone has regrouped, Nicole will die. The sound of the alarm going off in that bank may as well have been the Grim Reaper tolling his bell. It almost feels like this is the canonical way things should go, though. Jason and Lucia’s tale is one of escape, with tragedy, twists, and treachery meeting them at each turn. The Cartel Heist is no different when played this way. It’s pure action thriller filmmaking. Heat, Thief, Ocean's Eleven, The Town, Speed. It has the lot.

Not only is this mission fantastic from a storytelling perspective, but it’s also a feast of level design. Yes, it may largely take place on rails, but there’s enough wiggle room there for you to change tracks and give the impression of player agency, even when there seems to be little of it on the surface. Under the hood, the gears are always ticking, some of which have been greased hours previously, primed and ready to slot into place. There’s never a dull moment, whether that be in a tense first half soundtracked by the ticking of the clock, or in its balls-to-the-wall explosive second section.

Gunfights, safe-cracking, car chases — it has all the gameplay ingredients needed to be considered Rockstar’s greatest ever heist, and perhaps mission full stop. I just find it fascinating that if you happened to do it perfectly, you might not see what the fuss is all about.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: Here's When and Where to Stream Every NFL Football Game on Thanksgiving
articles.body:
Trying to stream live sporting events in 2026 has become a chore in itself, with so many networks and streaming services holding exclusive rights for the various leagues or even specific games. Thanksgiving and the NFL have been an annual holiday tradition dating back to 1934, when the Detroit Lions hosted the Chicago Bears in a nationally televised game. This year is no different, as three major games will be televised across the major TV networks and streaming services. Check out the full schedule below, including where you can stream each of the Thanksgiving NFL games today.

Where to Stream Every Thanksgiving NFL Game Today

As is tradition, there are a slew of games taking place on the Thanksgiving holiday this year. The three games during Thanksgiving will be airing on local TV channels and the corresponding streaming services, as well as any of the major live TV steaming services that include local channels. Some streaming services even offer free trials , so you can stream the football games, and more, at no cost.

Here's the full schedule for Thursday, November 26:

Game 1: Chicago Bears at Detroit Lions @ 10:00 AM PT

The morning game between the Lions and Bears is airing on CBS, which means it will be available to stream on Paramount+ . It's currently marked down to $2.99 for the first two months for Black Friday, so you can subscribe for the game and stay for some movies and TV shows.

While Paramount+ no longer offers a free trial, there is a workaround you can take advantage of. Walmart+ offers a free trial that includes Paramount+ as an added benefit, so you can get groceries delivered and watch the game.

Game 2: Philadelphia Eagles at Dallas Cowboys @ 1:30 PM PT

The NFC East division matchup between the Cowboys and Eagles will be airing on FOX networks. If you're looking to stream the game, you can catch it on FOX One, which is discounted to $4.99 for the first month as part of a Black Friday deal .

Alternatively, this is the only game that will technically be available to stream for free through Tubi, which you can watch online or through the Tubi app. All it requires is signing up for a free Tubi account and you're good to go.

Game 3: Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills @ 5:20 PM PT

The evening game between the Bills and Chiefs will be airing on NBC and available to stream on Peacock or the NFL+ app on your phone or tablet. You can sign up for three months of Peacock Select for just $2.99 (or $29.99 for the year) as part of a Black Friday deal .

Peacock doesn't have a free trial anymore, but like Paramount+, you can try it out for free by signing up for a Walmart+ free trial .

Are any of the NFL Thanksgiving games worth watching?

The biggest game you won't want to miss this Thanksgiving is between the Bills (9-1) and Chiefs (8-2). Both teams are at the top of the respective divisions and are vying for the #1 seed in the NFL playoffs. Buffalo is coming in hot, winning its last six games and averaging 31 points per game.

Bills QB Josh Allen and Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes have faced each other a total of 10 times in their careers, splitting the wins for a 5-5 record against one another. There are definitely playoff vibes for this game, and thankfully Turkey Time should be over by the time it starts, so you can relax, digest, and enjoy the matchup.

The morning game is also one to watch as the Lions and Bears are battling for the top of the NFC North division, with both teams sharing an 8-2 record. The Lions enter with a six-game winning streak and are undefeated at home this season, while Chicago has been on a five-game tear ever since QB Caleb Williams returned from a hamstring injury. Should be a good one.

Unfortunately, the midday game might be a bit of a snoozer as both the Cowboys and Eagles are under .500 this season, but divisional matchups are always at least a little exciting, right?

Matthew Adler has written for IGN since 2019 covering all things gaming, tech, tabletop games, and more. You can follow him on the site formerly known as Twitter @MatthewAdler and watch him stream on Twitch .

articles.title: Every Current Model Apple Watch Has Dropped to New Price Lows for Black Friday
articles.summary: Starts at just $179 for a brand new watch.
articles.body:
The Apple Watch is essentially a natural extension of your iPhone and anyone who uses an iPhone, in my opinion, could benefit from an Apple Watch. If you've shied away because of the cost, then these Black Friday deals might change your mind. Every new model - the Apple Watch SE 3, Apple Watch Series 12, and the Apple Watch Ultra 4 - have all dropped to the lowest prices of the year on Amazon. This is a great opportunity to see what you've been missing out.

Black Friday Deal: Apple Watch SE 3 for $179

The latest generation Apple Watch SE just dropped to its lowest price ever. For Black Friday, Amazon is offering the Apple Watch SE 3 starting at just $179 with free shipping for the 40mm model after a 30% off instant discount. The Apple Watch SE has nearly all of the essential watch, tracker, and fitness functions of the Apple Watch Series 12 at nearly half the price.

The Apple Watch SE 3 was released back in September of 2025. It's Apple's least expensive Apple Watch. Despite its low price tag, it's stylish and boasts great build quality with a 100% recycled aluminum case and Ion-X scratch resistant glass face. It comes in both 40mm and 44mm case sizes. The always-on Retina OLED LTPO display features a pixel density of 326ppi and up to 1,000 nits of peak brightness. The Apple Watch SE uses the same S10 processor used in the Apple Watch Series 11 , which is only one generation older. The only difference is that the Apple Watch SE isn't equipped with the second gen Ultra Wideband chip for Precision Finding.

Black Friday Deal: Apple Watch Series 12 for $299

The Apple Watch Series 12 , which was released in September 2026, has also hit a new price low. The base 42mm GPS model just dropped below $300 for the first time since its launch. The Series 12 comes with a host of incremental upgrades including the S11 processor, Health Sensing System heart rate chcker, Audio Intelligence, and more.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is the best smartwatch for most iOS users . It's stylish, boasts excellent build quality, and seamlessly integrates with your iPhone. It's loaded with tons of practical health and fitness features, including activity tracking and heart rate monitoring. There are a number of notable upgrades over the previous generation model. The biggest one is the new Apple S11 chip with 4GB of RAM. Also new to the Series 12 is Audio Intelligence, which can automatically identify sounds and music as well as record and recap conversations. Other upgrades include a Health Sensing System that checks your heart rate every 5 seconds, HRV tracking, and daily "Readiness" score.

Black Friday Deal: Apple Watch Ultra 4 for $650

The Apple Watch Ultra 4 was also released on September 18 alongside the Series 12. It's $150 off for Black Friday and is the first major discount I've seen for Apple's newest flagship watch. Upgrades over the previous generation include a newer S11 chip with increased 4GB of RAM and longer 50-hour battery life. Like the Apple Watch Series 12, the Ultra now supports Audio Intelligence and the Health Sensing System with "Readiness" score. It still features the same 49mm titanium case, 1.89" always-on Retina LTPO3 OLED display with 3,000nits of peak brightness protected by a sapphire crystal face, and 100m water resistance.

Can you use an Apple Watch with Android phones?

Although it's technically possible to use an Apple Watch with an Android phone, we wouldn't recommend it. Apple made it so that a lot of the functionality of the Apple Watch requires a smartphone with an iOS operating system. There are some workarounds to implement some of its features, but for the average person, the hassle is not worth it. If you're absolutely intent on getting an Apple Watch, then getting an iPhone first would be the best option.
